The mapping is `ESCALATION_BY_KIND` in `apps/api/src/tools/defineTmsTool.ts`. It is a `Record<TmsErrorKind, EscalationTrigger | null>` with one row for each of the nine `TmsError` kinds. A kind with no row fails `npm run typecheck`, and FR-046 and FR-047 describe this as an exhaustive mapping with no default case.

Only two TMS error kinds escalate:
- `unavailable` (a 5xx response) marks the `tms_unavailable` trigger.
- `timeout` marks the `tms_timeout` trigger.

The other seven kinds map to `null`, so they carry and mark no escalation. From the `get_booking_status` error table, those include `not_found`, `rate_limited`, `network`, `invalid_response`, `unauthorized` and `forbidden`. I did not read the rest of the table, so I can't name the seventh kind.

Separately, the `get_booking_status` tool escalates a `customer_scope_conflict` for a data-integrity conflict on the order path. That is not a TMS error kind.
